findings.summary: CheckForInvalidColorData is ported as `validate`, but only test harnesses call it. The production render path never does, so an invalid colour on discrete targets is not corrected. Discrete leaves go dark and full-colour leaves in the same target keep the uncorrected colour. The golden suite hides this because its harness calls validate itself.
findings.csharp: upstream/Vixen/src/Vixen.Core/Module/Effect/EffectModuleInstanceBase.cs:53-67: the TargetNodes setter calls TargetNodesChanged (line 62). Vixen.Modules/Effect/SetLevel/SetLevel.cs:21-24 calls CheckForInvalidColorData from TargetNodesChanged, and SetLevel.cs:48-57 calls it from the ModuleData setter. SetLevel.cs:114-126 then does `Color = validColors.First()`, which writes the corrected value into _data, so it also persists on save.
findings.rust: crates/fx-basic/src/set_level.rs:7 and :36-40 define and register `validate`. The only callers in crates/ and app/Sources are crates/vixen-effects/src/testing.rs:68 and crates/vixen-effect-registry/tests/golden.rs:396. crates/vixen-engine/src/render.rs:44-45 calls `render(&ctx, job.params)` directly on immutable params, and crates/vixen-io/src/sequence.rs:462 and :466 build params without validating.
findings.scenario: New Set Level with default White on a SingleColor red relay such as the owner's 'Color Bottom'. C#: corrected to red, intent is StaticDiscrete red at level 1 (golden case discrete/defaults). Rust engine path, run in a scratch probe: colour stays white, the leaf is skipped, 0 intents, dark. Group [red discrete, full colour] with default White: C# gives Discrete red plus Lighting red. Rust engine path gives only Lighting white. The same applies when an effect is moved onto a discrete row. Existing files are unaffected today: a survey of all 9781 Set Level effects found 0 saved colours invalid for their target.

findings.summary: Upstream compares discrete colours with System.Drawing.Color equality, which also compares known-colour state and name. The Rust compares ARGB channels only. A discrete element whose colour property holds a known colour such as Color.RoyalBlue is always dark under Set Level in upstream C#, but lit in Rust. The owner's current data does not reach this.
findings.csharp: Vixen.Modules/Property/Color/ColorSetupHelper.cs:26-27 and :54 store the panel's default known colour (ColorPanel.cs:35-37 returns it unchanged). Vixen.Modules/Property/Color/ColorProperty.cs:174 and :178 add stored colours to the HashSet as they are. Vixen.Core/Common/ColorSpaces.cs:311-317 makes RGB.ToArgb an unnamed FromArgb. SetLevel.cs:119 and :139 call Contains on that set. Run on .NET 10: `new HashSet<Color>{Color.RoyalBlue}.Contains(Color.FromArgb(65,105,225))` is False.
findings.rust: crates/vixen-core/src/color.rs:3-9: Color derives PartialEq over the four channels, and its comment says Vixen never relies on the distinction. crates/vixen-io/src/values.rs:56-66 maps known colours to plain ARGB, and crates/vixen-io/src/system.rs decode_color (from line 378) reads SingleColor through it. crates/fx-basic/src/set_level.rs:23 and :37 then compare channels.
findings.scenario: Element configured with ColorSetupHelper's untouched RoyalBlue default (state=1, knownColor set), Set Level default White. Upstream C#: colour is corrected to (65,105,225), then `colors.Contains(Color)` is False, the leaf is skipped, and the element is dark. Rust (scratch probe): StaticDiscrete (65,105,225) at level 1, lit. The owner's 10 SingleColor properties and both colour sets are all state=2, so their show is unaffected. The golden suite cannot catch this: tools/golden/Golden.csproj links a modified C# build whose outputs/Vixen/src/Vixen.Modules/Property/Color/ColorProperty.cs:165 and :169 canonicalise to FromArgb, which differs from upstream.

findings.summary: A childless node with no Element inside the target throws NullReferenceException in C#, leaving the whole effect dark. The Rust skips that one leaf and lights the others.
findings.csharp: Vixen.Core/Sys/ElementNode.cs:258-266 yields any childless node as a leaf, even with a null Element. Vixen.Core/IO/Xml/Serializer/XmlElementNodeSerializer.cs:95 creates such a node when a file has a node with no channelId and no children. SetLevel.cs:145 evaluates `elementNode.Element.Id`, which throws. EffectModuleInstanceBase.cs:132-138 catches and logs it, and _elementData stays the empty set from SetLevel.cs:28.
findings.rust: crates/fx-basic/src/set_level.rs:26: `let Some(element) = ctx.tree.node(leaf).element_id else { continue };` skips only that leaf. crates/vixen-io/src/system.rs:319 creates the same childless node with element_id None.
findings.scenario: Set Level default on group [A, EmptyGroup (no channelId, no children), B]. C#, run through the compiled effect: PreRender=False, NullReferenceException logged, 0 elements with intents, everything dark. Rust (scratch probe): A and B lit at White level 1. PORTING_GUIDE.md says a C# exception means the effect stays dark, so the Rust should render nothing for this target. Not reached by the owner's data: their SystemConfig has 0 childless nodes without a channel.

findings.summary: The effect's Information text is missing from the Rust descriptor, which carries only the link. The C# effect editor shows this text in a panel above a More Info link.
findings.csharp: SetLevel.cs:101-104 returns "Visit the Vixen Lights website for more information on this effect." Vixen.Modules/Editor/EffectEditor/EffectPropertyEditorGrid.cs:295 reads it. Vixen.Modules/Editor/EffectEditor/Design/CategorizedLayout.xaml:55-67 shows it in a panel when non-empty, with the More Info link.
findings.rust: crates/vixen-effects/src/framework.rs:481-510: EffectDescriptor has `info_link` (line 492) but no information text. crates/fx-basic/src/generated/set_level.rs:15 has only INFO_LINK, and scripts/gen_effect_params.py:631 extracts only InformationLink.
findings.scenario: Opening a Set Level in the effect editor: C# shows the sentence plus More Info below the properties. An editor driven by the Rust table has no text to show. The sentence is generic for Set Level, but Strobe and the layering effects use different text, so it cannot simply be hardcoded. No Rust effect editor exists yet, so this only affects future UI work.

areas_checked: Overall result: the render logic matches upstream. The four findings are one production wiring gap, two edge cases the owner's data does not reach, and one piece of editor metadata.

Rendering, read line by line: SetLevel.cs _PreRender/RenderNode against set_level.rs render. Covers last target wins, Distinct leaf order, the discrete skip test, Static vs Discrete intent choice, zero start time, duration, cancellation returning the previous result, and no state kept between renders.

Golden run: the already-built golden binary for set_level passed 41 cases and 28818 frame values with 0 mismatches and 0 default problems. Unit tests set_level::tests also pass. No project files were built or changed.

Golden caveat: tools/golden links a modified C# build, not upstream. outputs/Vixen/src/.../SetLevel.cs:38 uses `_elementData.Add(RenderNode(node))` where upstream SetLevel.cs:36 assigns, and that build's ColorProperty.cs canonicalises colours. EffectNodeSurrogate and PreRender cancellation differ too. No SetLevel golden case has two targets or a named colour, so the data does not contradict upstream, but it cannot detect set_level-2.

Hand-worked parameter sets, all matching. (1) White, level 1, SingleColor white leaf, 650 ms: StaticDiscrete white 1.0, active 0..650 ms inclusive. (2) RGB (1, 0.5, 0), level 0.333, full colour: Math.Round(127.5)=128, same as round_ties_even, Lighting (255,128,0) 0.333. (3) Zero-length: 0/0 ticks is NaN, the interpolator rejects it, default value (golden L00000000,0), same in percent_of. (4) Level 1.5, -0.25 and NaN: Lighting clamps to 1, 0 and NaN; Discrete clips to 1, 0 and 0. Levels -0.25 and NaN were confirmed by running both implementations; 1.5 by the golden over-range case (Lighting) and by reading clip_value (Discrete).

Intent timing: NonSegmentedLinearIntent and Interpolator (percent inside 0..1 inclusive) against Intent::state_at/percent_of; IntentNode against Rust IntentNode; TimeNode.IntersectsInclusively and _RemoveExpiredEffects (time > EndTime) against schedule.rs inclusive hi. No difference.

Value types: RGB ctor, ToArgb and implicit conversions against Rgb::new/from_color/to_color; LightingValue HSV.Clamp against clamp; DiscreteValue XYZ.ClipValue against clip_value; FullColorWithAlpha and FullColorWithAplha. Out-of-range stored RGB would throw in C# FromArgb and saturate in Rust, which the porting guide treats as deliberate, and the real data has none.

Discrete handling: getValidColorsForElementNode order (own colours, then depth-first with first occurrence kept) against collect_valid_colors/push_unique, so validColors.First() equals valid[0]; isElementNodeDiscreteColored; HasDiscreteColors from all targets. Only named-colour equality differs (set_level-2). C# caches HasDiscreteColors at target assignment and Rust recomputes per render, which is not visible in any flow that exists in the Rust today.

Parameter table: all three entries match. TargetPositioning: base member, level 0, ns VixenModules.Effect.Effect, not browsable, default Strings, enum labels Strings/Locations. color: Rgb, category Color order 1, label Color, description 'Controls the color of the effect.', default (1,1,1). level: Double, category Brightness order 2, label Intensity, description 'Controls the brightness of the effect.', Editor::Level, default 1. Labels and categories were checked against the three resx files. XML order and namespaces were checked against real .tim files. Absent members read as default(T), since DataContractSerializer skips constructors.

Descriptor fields: type id, name, group, author, description, version, data type and namespace, info link and icon path all match. No descriptor overrides for media, marks or property dependencies apply. SetLevelData's constructor only sets level and color; no helper call.
Visibility: SetLevel has no UpdateAttributes or SetBrowsable calls, and `visibility: None` is correct. Display order Color then Intensity matches.
Property setters: IntensityLevel and Color only store the value and set IsDirty/OnPropertyChanged, so `param_changed: None` is correct.
Validation logic itself: `validate` matches CheckForInvalidColorData apart from colour equality; the gap is in who calls it (set_level-1).

Thumbnails: SetLevel has no GenerateVisualRepresentation override and no ForceGenerateVisualRepresentation, so `visual: None` and `force_visual: false` are correct. EffectRasterizer/IntentRasterizer against thumbnail.rs was read for the static lighting and discrete intents; no difference for this effect. The DisableEffectsEditorRendering fallback is an app-wide setting, not specific to this effect, and has no Rust side to compare.

Panic review: empty targets, childless nodes, zero-length spans, single-element targets, a non-parsing value (reads as Color::EMPTY or 0.0) and valid[0] (guarded) cannot panic. Parameter names all exist. No crash risk found.

Real data survey, read-only, of all .tim files in the owner's show: 9781 Set Level effects, every one with exactly 1 target, TargetPositioning Strings, level 1.0, non-zero span, no missing targets, no out-of-range or non-byte RGB. 9719 effects target discrete SingleColor leaves; 62 target full-colour groups. Colours in use: white, red, blue, (10,255,0), black, (189,87,23), (120,61,0). 0 effects need colour correction. The tree has 1136 nodes, 0 shared nodes and 0 childless nodes without an element.

Not findings. Multiple targets: upstream EffectNodeSurrogate.cs loads only the first target, while Rust keeps all and render uses the last, but no code maps file targets to render jobs yet and the real data always has one target. PulseRenderer: Set Level does not use it. The effect editor's discrete colour picker and level slider have no Rust UI to compare against.

Scratch probes, outside the project: /tmp/vixen-scratch/survey_set_level.py, /tmp/vixen-scratch/rsprobe.rs and /tmp/vixen-scratch/csprobe/src/Program.cs. Other agents were changing crates during this review; validate callers were re-checked at the end, and set_level.rs, generated/set_level.rs and render.rs had not changed.
